summary.text: Cole Birkeland is the Democratic candidate for Minnesota House of Representatives District 41A in the November 3, 2026 general election, challenging Republican incumbent Wayne Johnson; the Democratic primary was canceled.
An attorney, he says he previously worked as a city attorney for local governments in the Twin Cities area.

paragraphs.text: Cole Birkeland earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Northwestern, St. Paul and a law degree from the University of Minnesota Law School, according to Ballotpedia.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he currently works as an attorney representing people to protect their retirement savings and civil rights, and that he previously worked as a city attorney with local governments across the Twin Cities metro area.

He said he coordinates service projects as director of community service for the Lake Elmo Rotary Club, co-authored a report about improving emergency medical services in Minnesota, and lectures students about the Constitution and civic responsibility.
Birkeland's survey named rising costs, accountability and oversight in government, and building bridges across the aisle among his campaign's key messages.
He wrote that he supports more severe penalties for fraud and a full audit of state government programs.
